question: Which categories of machinery always require a conformity assessment procedure involving a notified body?
text: The passages do not identify which machinery categories always require a notified body. Recital 59 of the Machinery Regulation only says that higher-risk 'certain categories' need a stricter procedure, so the specific list must be checked in the Regulation's annexes, which are not provided.

question: Which conformity assessment procedures can the manufacturer choose for machinery listed in Annex I, Part A?
value: EU type-examination (module B) followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C)
conformity based on full quality assurance (module H)
conformity based on unit verification (module G)
text: For machinery in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer may choose one of three procedures under Regulation Article 25(2): module B followed by module C, module H, or module G.

steps.quote: Where the category of machinery or related product is listed in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer or the natural or legal person referred to in Article 18 shall apply one of the following procedures: (a) EU type-examination (module B) set out in Annex VII, followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C) set out in Annex VIII; (b) conformity based on full quality assurance (module H) set out in Annex IX; (c) conformity based on unit verification (module G) set out in Annex X.

question: Which category does a safety component with self-evolving behaviour based on machine learning fall under?
value: Annex I, Part A, point 5 of the REG Regulation: safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions.
text: Under the REG Regulation, Annex I, Part A, point 5 covers safety components with fully or partially self-evolving machine-learning behaviour that ensure safety functions. Recital 54 explains that these require third-party conformity assessment.

steps.text: Read on demand: REG, Annex I, Part A, point 5
steps.quote: 5. Safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions.
steps.locator: REG, Annex I, Part A, point 5

steps.quote: Therefore, the conformity assessment of a safety component or a system with self-evolving behaviour ensuring safety functions should be carried out by a third party, whether or not the safety component has been placed independently on the market or is part of a system embedded in machinery that is placed on the market.

question: When must guards for moving transmission parts be interlocking movable guards instead of fixed guards?
value: Interlocking movable guards must be used where frequent access is envisaged.
text: Under Annex III, section 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards where frequent access is envisaged; otherwise fixed guards under section 1.4.2.1 may be used. The earlier Directive (Annex I, 1.3.8.1) says 'should' rather than 'shall' for the same condition.

steps.text: Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.3.8.1
steps.quote: Interlocking movable guards shall be used where frequent access is envisaged.

steps.text: Read on demand: DIR, Annex I, 1.3.8.1
steps.quote: Interlocking movable guards should be used where frequent access is envisaged.

question: Who is considered the manufacturer after a substantial modification of machinery?
value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery or related product is considered the manufacturer (REG Art. 18), except a non-professional user modifying for their own use.
text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation (REG), any natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product is considered its manufacturer, unless it is a non-professional user modifying the machinery for their own use.

steps.quote: A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation

A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation

question: A machine was built and its EC declaration of conformity signed on 10 January 2027, but it is made available on the Union market for the first time on 25 January 2027. Which act governs its placing on the market: Directive 2006/42/EC or Regulation (EU) 2023/1230?
value: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 governs, because the machine is first placed on the market on 25 January 2027, after the 20 January 2027 date and outside the Directive 2006/42/EC transitional protection.
text: Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 54, applies from 20 January 2027, and the Article 52(1) transitional protection for Directive 2006/42/EC covers only products placed on the market before that date, so this machine falls under the Regulation.

steps.text: Read on demand: REG, Art. 54 (corrected by the corrigendum (Corrigendum, point 10: '14 January 2027' now reads '20 January 2027'; Corrigendum, point 11: '14 January 2024' now reads '20 January 2024'; Corrigendum, point 12: '14 October 2023' now reads '20 October 2026'; Corrigendum, point 13: '13 July 2023' now reads '19 July 2023'; Corrigendum, point 14: '14 July 2024' now reads '20 July 2024'))

steps.quote: Member States shall not impede the making available on the market of products which were placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027.

question: On 1 December 2026 the manufacturer of a machine in a category listed in Annex IV to Directive 2006/42/EC, not built to harmonised standards, wants to place it on the market using unit verification (module G) instead of EC type-examination or full quality assurance. Is that procedure admitted by the act applicable on that day?
text: Under Article 12(4) of Directive 2006/42/EC, Annex IV machinery not built to harmonised standards may use only EC type-examination plus internal checks, or full quality assurance, so module G is not admitted under that Directive. The passages do not state the date from which the Regulation applies or the date on which the Directive is repealed, so they do not establish whether the Directive or the Regulation governs on 1 December 2026.

question: On 1 December 2026, for Annex IV categories of Directive 2006/42/EC built to harmonised standards covering all the relevant requirements, the manufacturer may use internal checks on manufacture alone. text: The passages do not state which Annex IV categories of Directive 2006/42/EC lose internal production control (module A) on 1 February 2027. Article 25(3) of the Regulation sets the module A conditions for Annex I Part B categories, but no passage gives that date or the list of affected categories.

question: On 1 March 2027 a company that is neither the original manufacturer nor a non-professional user carries out a substantial modification of a machine placed on the market in February 2027. In what capacity (as which economic operator) does it answer for that machine under the act applicable on that day?
value: Manufacturer: the company takes on the obligations of the manufacturer (Article 10) for the machinery, under REG Article 18.
text: Under Article 18 of the Regulation (REG), a company that substantially modifies machinery is considered its manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations. The passages do not give the date from which the Regulation applies, so its applicability on 1 March 2027 is not confirmed by them.

steps.quote: A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10 for that machinery or related product

question: The UNIVPM equipment guideline states that the manufacturer is obliged to supply the instructions for use on paper. On 1 March 2027, for a machine intended only for professional users and placed on the market that day, may the manufacturer provide the instructions for use in digital format instead of on paper?
text: Yes. Under Article 10(7) of the Machinery Regulation, a professional-use machine may have its instructions for use provided in digital format, provided the manufacturer meets the conditions in points (a) to (c) of that article. The UNIVPM guideline's paper requirement is a company procedure and yields to the higher-ranking regulation.

steps.quote: The instructions may be provided in a digital format.

In the case of machinery or a related product intended for non-professional users or that can, under reasonably foreseeable conditions, be used by non-professional users, even if not intended for them, the manufacturer shall provide, in paper format, the safety information that is essential for putting the machinery or related product into service and for using it in a safe way.
